facts.raw_span: sudden-onset chest pain
history of diabetes
paroxysmal atrial fibrillation
Normal sinus rhythm
up to 2.0-mm ST-segment elevation in leads II, III, and aVF
subtle ST-segment elevation in leads V7-V9
1.0-mm to 2.0-mm downward-sloping ST-segment depression in leads V2-V4
R/S greater than 1 in leads V1-V2
Initial high-sensitive troponin T level: 0.309 ng/mL
thrombotic occlusion of the distal left circumflex artery
contrast present in the myocardium and pericardial effusion
blood pressure fell to 60/40 mm Hg

support_spans: up to 2.0-mm ST-segment elevation in leads II, III, and aVF
Initial high-sensitive troponin T level: 0.309 ng/mL
thrombotic occlusion of the distal left circumflex artery
concepts.why: The patient presented with sudden-onset chest pain, ST-segment elevation in leads II, III, and aVF, and a high-sensitive troponin T level, which are all indicative of an acute myocardial infarction, specifically an inferior wall MI due to the location of the ST-segment elevation and the thrombotic occlusion of the distal left circumflex artery.

support_spans: subtle ST-segment elevation in leads V7-V9
Initial high-sensitive troponin T level: 0.309 ng/mL
concepts.why: The patient presented with subtle ST-segment elevation in leads V7-V9, which is indicative of a posterior wall MI, and a high-sensitive troponin T level, which confirms myocardial damage.

support_spans: blood pressure fell to 60/40 mm Hg
thrombotic occlusion of the distal left circumflex artery
concepts.why: The patient developed cardiogenic shock, as evidenced by a significant drop in blood pressure, which is likely due to the thrombotic occlusion of the distal left circumflex artery and the resulting myocardial infarction.

concepts.preferred_label: Acute Coronary Syndrome with Cardiac Tamponade
concepts.why: The presence of ST-segment depression in leads V2-V4 and contrast present in the myocardium and pericardial effusion explains the uncovered finding of cardiac tamponade.
The R/S ratio greater than 1 in leads V1-V2 is indicative of right ventricular infarction.

rationales.F05: ST-segment elevation in leads II, III, and aVF is indicative of inferior myocardial infarction.
rationales.F06: ST-segment elevation in leads V7-V9 is indicative of posterior myocardial infarction.
rationales.F09: Elevated troponin T level is indicative of myocardial infarction.
rationales.F10: Thrombotic occlusion of the distal left circumflex artery is indicative of acute coronary syndrome.
rationales.F11: Contrast present in the myocardium and pericardial effusion is indicative of cardiac tamponade.
rationales.F12: Hypotension is indicative of cardiogenic shock.
